<span id="a2399c88"></span>
# Event tracking planning

Before integrating the SDK, you need to perform event tracking planning based on your business analysis, and clarify what events and attributes may require event tracking in the business indicators to be analyzed. When planning event tracking, you need to understand some basic concepts and pre\-information such as event tracking events and properties preset by DataFinder, DataFinder's user identity logic, etc., and combine the capabilities provided by DataFinder to plan event tracking.

<span id="53f52e34"></span>
## Basic concept


|Basic concept |Concept note |Event tracking planning and SDK integration points |Detailed guidance document |
|---|---|---|---|
|Event, event properties, event public properties, user properties |DataFinder's user behavior data analytics is based on event + user model.<br><br><br>* Event & Event Attributes: A certain or a type of behavior of the user is called an "event". Event attributes are information such as the form and location of the event that are collected synchronously when the event is triggered to describe the event. For example, if a user purchases a product, then the user's behavior event is "Purchase", and the event attributes are "Product Name", "Product Classification", "Payment Amount", etc .<br><br>* Event public attributes: Attributes that are not strongly associated with an event and that are common to multiple or all events, such as the version number of the application, device information, and so on.<br><br>* User & User Attribute: User refers to the person who is the subject of the event behavior. User attributes refer to attributes of the user's own status (independent of behavior, such as age, gender, etc.) or user\-related attributes that are related to behavior but do not change frequently (such as VIP level, registration time, etc.). |You need to plan the events, event attributes, and user attributes to be collected according to the needs of business analysis. When integrating the SDK |See the detailed concept introduction [Data Model](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Model). |
|Event tracking, full event tracking, custom event tracking |* Event tracking: Through the development of the SDK, the process of writing event logic into the code is called **event tracking**. DataFinder provides you with preset events and event properties, such events and event properties do not require you to manually event tracking, just turn on the capture switch.<br><br>* Full event tracking: is a kind of preset event and event properties provided by DataFinder. In DataFinder, the full event tracking events collected are bav2b_click button clicks and bav2b_page page browsing. No additional investment in research and development is required, but it will be at the expense of reporting a large amount of data, and only simple PV and UV can be collected, which is a bit'powerless' for the collection of rich business data.<br><br>* Code event tracking: Code event tracking refers to the development engineer who manually writes the code to implement the data collection logic according to the personalized needs of the business. Wide collection range and flexible application. However, it requires investment in research and development and requires certain technical capabilities. |It is usually recommended that you combine the preset events/properties provided by DataFinder with custom event tracking for event tracking planning. |[Event Tracking, Full Event Tracking](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Tracking_Full_Event_Tracking) |


<span id="0dfd2056"></span>
## Understanding data reporting requirements (format, quantity restrictions, etc.)

When planning for event tracking, you need to be clear about the data format requirements of the events and attributes to be collected and reported, as well as some restrictions on collection and reporting, so as to avoid subsequent failure to meet the requirements due to data formats, which will lead to data collection that cannot be warehoused and cannot be queried and analyzed later.

The data reported by the SDK usually has a fixed format, mainly including `user`, `header`, and `events`.


|Field |Effect |Mini Program Data Sample |
|---|---|---|
|`user` |Store user attribute data, such as web_id, user_unique_id these important attributes. |```TypeScript```<br>```[```<br>```  {```<br>```    events: [```<br>```      {```<br>```        event: 'app_launch',```<br>```        params: '{"path":"pages/index/index",……}',```<br>```        local_time_ms: 1745897787714,```<br>```        session_id: 'd8b28410-6079-42da-***',```<br>```      },```<br>```      {```<br>```        event: 'predefine_pageview',```<br>```        params: '{"scene":1001,……}',```<br>```        local_time_ms: 1745897787756,```<br>```        session_id: 'd8b28410-6079-42da-9f91-5a49d6ffb01f',```<br>```      },```<br>```    ],```<br>```    user: {```<br>```      web_id: '7498573*****',```<br>```      user_unique_id: 'zhangsan',```<br>```    },```<br>```    header: {```<br>```      app_id: 0,```<br>```      app_version: '',```<br>```      os_name: 'devtools',```<br>```      os_version: 'iOS 10.0.1',```<br>```      // ……```<br>```      custom: {```<br>```        custom_platform: 'miniProduct',```<br>```        mp_platform: '0',```<br>```        mp_platform_app_version: '8.0.5',```<br>```        // ……```<br>```      },```<br>```      // ……,```<br>```    },```<br>```  },```<br>```]```<br> |
|`header` |Store event public properties.<br><br>app_id, os_name These are preset and will be placed directly under the header. If it is the event public property you customize, it will be placed under header.custom. ||
|`events` |Store events and event properties.<br><br>It is an array that supports carrying multiple events.<br><br>Each event has event, params, local_time_ms, session_id fields, where local_time_ms, session_id are automatically generated by the SDK, and event, params are set by the business, event is the event name, and params stores the event attribute (the value is that the JSON object is serialized). ||


Among them, when you need to report custom events and custom properties, you need to ensure that the data format of events and attributes meets the requirements. Please refer to the data format requirements and data reporting restrictions supported by the current DataFinder [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

Common problem:

* The data type transmission at each end is inconsistent, how does the system handle it? How to modify?[Q2: The data type transmission at each end is inconsistent. How does the system handle it? How to modify it?](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification#q2%EF%BC%9A-%E5%90%84%E7%AB%AF%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E7%B1%BB%E5%9E%8B%E4%BC%A0%E8%BE%93%E4%B8%8D%E4%B8%80%E8%87%B4%EF%BC%8C%E7%B3%BB%E7%BB%9F%E5%A6%82%E4%BD%95%E5%A4%84%E7%90%86%EF%BC%9F%E5%A6%82%E4%BD%95%E4%BF%AE%E6%94%B9%EF%BC%9F)


<span id="9fd87708"></span>
## Understanding user identity logic

When planning for event tracking, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder, which is used to combine the user identity logic of your own business to eventually unify the source of user identity data. DataFinder defaults to the **user** as the object of statistical analysis, and defaults to using ssid as the user's unique identification ID to calculate the index. At this time, the user's SSID is the default statistical caliber. When your analysis object is a user, it is recommended to keep the default statistical caliber ssid, DataFinder can ID_Mapping the user's device_id/web_id, user_unique_id, etc. mapping, try to restore a real user individual through a ssid.


* **device_id**, **web_id**, **anonymous_id:**  Can be used as the unique ID of the device, mostly in scenarios where the user's real name ID cannot be obtained.

* **user_unique_id:**  It is the login user ID, which is mostly used in the scenario where the user's real\-name ID can be obtained. Generally, the user ID used in the product business is directly used, such as the login account. When the user_unique_id is not set, in the SaaS version, the system will automatically use device_id/web_id instead.

* **Ssid:**  for the DataFinder user statistics caliber ID, with the device identification device_id/web_id, login state user identification user_unique_id mutual Mapping, can ensure that the user anonymity and real\-name ID unified state.


See the mapping logic for the three types of IDs and more information about user identities [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers).

## Understand the preset events and properties supported by the Mini Program

As mentioned above, in most business analysis scenarios, you need to combine your own business characteristics for custom event tracking planning and integration. Before that, you can first understand the preset events and preset properties currently provided by DataFinder, and combine the existing preset events and attribute capabilities to further plan the requirements for custom code event tracking.


* See the list of preset events and properties supported on the Mini Program side [Mini Program Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_Preset_Events_and_Properties).

* At the same time, you also need to pay attention to the currently disabled preset attribute list. When planning custom event tracking and attributes in the future, you need to avoid the same name as the disabled attribute, otherwise the data will not be reported normally. See for details [Disable Properties List](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Disable_Properties_List).

# Preparation

<span id="f4224eb3"></span>
## Step 1 (optional): Create event tracking requirements/Enter custom event tracking

After completing the event tracking planning, it is recommended that you create the event tracking requirements according to the planning and then enter the custom event tracking into the DataFinder to complete the warehousing of the custom event tracking in the DataFinder metadata.


* Event tracking request management: You can manage event tracking requirements through DataFinder's event tracking request management function, and you can continue to maintain and manage requirements in the event tracking request management page to improve management efficiency. See the operation to create event tracking request management [Request Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Request_Management).

* Custom event tracking entry: You can first create custom event tracking metadata into the DataFinder according to the event tracking plan. For activity details, see [New event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6), [Add event properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Properties#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7), [Add user properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_Properties#533b53ea).


<span id="8c5ac3ed"></span>
## Step 2: Obtain the APPID


* In the SaaS\-cloud native scenario, you can find the corresponding application in "Project Center" \> "Project Management" \> "Project Details", click "Access Data", and view the application ID (APPID) and APP URL of the application in the application details. For details, please refer to [Project Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Project_Management__).

## Step 3: Obtain the reporting address and configure the Mini Program whitelist

When reporting data access, you need to confirm your data reporting address according to the current environment type and terminal type, and add the data reporting address to the "request legal domain name" in the background of the Mini Program. If the reporting address is set incorrectly, you will not be able to report and query the data normally in the future.

<span id="c60485e9"></span>

## Step2: Initialize the SDK: Based on the Mini Program native platform

When initializing the SDK, you usually need to call the core API of the SDK (init, config, event, etc.) to collect and report preset events and attribute data, collect and report custom events and data, and define user ID identification fields.

It is generally recommended to refer to the following process when integrating the Mini Program SDK :


|Import and initialize \-\-\- \> Report preset events \-\-\- \> Report custom events \-\-\- \> Set custom user \-\-\- \> Set report domain name |
|---|

In real scenarios, this value is generally obtained from the service interface of the business.```<br>```        $$sdk.config({```<br>```            user_unique_id: 'zhangsan'```<br>```        });```<br>```    }```<br>```});```<br><br><br>```TypeScript```<br>```const app = getApp()```<br>``````<br>```Component({```<br>```    data: {```<br>```        //...```<br>```    },```<br>```    methods: {```<br>```        bindViewTap() { //Call the event interface to report custom events and event properties```<br>```            app.$$sdk.event('test', {```<br>```                abc: 123,```<br>```            });```<br>```        }```<br>```    }```<br>```});```<br> |

   * Init: Initialize the SDK instance. The init interface needs to specify the appid information of the data report, and configure whether to turn on the log and other initialization parameters. <span id="de8981da"></span>
### Reporting customs events

According to the event tracking plan, if you need to collect and report custom events, you can call the "event" method to set the custom event name and event properties.

Usually we may need to report custom events on multiple pages of the Mini Program. For the convenience of using the SDK instance $$sdk on other pages of the Mini Program, consider mounting the SDK instance $$sdk on the App object. For example, to report a custom event on a page (such as pages/index/index.ts in the demo example), you can get the global object through getApp, then use the $$sdk mounted on it and call the event method.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|1. Initialize in the main entry file (app.ts file in the demo), similar to the above steps, and additionally mount the SDK instance $$sdk onto the App object.<br><br>   ```TypeScript```<br>```   import $$sdk from '@datarangers/sdk-mp';```<br>```   ```<br>```   $$sdk.init({```<br>```       //Please change to your own app_id```<br>```       app_id: 0,```<br>```       log: true,```<br>```       auto_report: true,```<br>```   });```<br>```   $$sdk.send();```<br>```   ```<br>```   App({```<br>```       $$sdk,```<br>```       //...```<br>```   });```<br>```   ```<br>   <br><br>2. In a separate page (where type.ts is newly created), use the $$sdk mounted in the main entry file and call the event method to report custom events and event properties.<br><br>   ```TypeScript```<br>```   const app = getApp()```<br>```   ```<br>```   Component({```<br>```       data: {```<br>```           //...```<br>```       },```<br>```       methods: {```<br>```           bindViewTap() {```<br>```               app.$$sdk.event('test', {```<br>```                   abc: 123,```<br>```               });```<br>```           }```<br>```       }```<br>```   });```<br>```   ```<br>    |<video src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/dd2d7102abb94489b6890b5b3781d627~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" controls></video><br> |



* Operation points:

   * If the project itself is a Typescript type and you encounter type problems when mounting $$sdk on the app, you can consider extending the type, such as creating a new type.d.ts type file for easy use everywhere, where the type definition is similar to this. (This extension type handling is not necessary, unless the project's type requirements directly affect the compilation.)

      ```TypeScript
      import SDK from '@datarangers/sdk-mp/sdk.d';
      export type NewIAppOption = IAppOption & {
        $$sdk: SDK,
      }
      ```
      

* Involving the core API:

   * Event: Use the event method to report custom events. This method supports single event mode and batch event mode reporting. The above is an example of a single event reporting. For more event interface parameter descriptions and usage examples, please see [event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#68e73ad4).

* More scene practice references:

   * [Set event public properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice#19a0bfde)


<span id="bb21600c"></span>
### Set up a custom user

If you need to set a custom user, you can call the config method to set user_unique_id properties.

Usually, when a user needs to log in with a real name, the business will use an ID to uniquely identify the user. You can report the user ID of the corresponding business through the config method and report it as the value of the user_unique_id. Usually, this value can be obtained through the service interface, or an existing fixed user identification ID value can be directly read. The following fixed value is reported as an example.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|```TypeScript```<br>```import $$sdk from '@datarangers/sdk-mp';```<br>``````<br>```$$sdk.init({```<br>```    //Please change to your own app_id```<br>```    app_id: 0,```<br>```    log: true,```<br>```    auto_report: true,```<br>```});```<br>```$$sdk.send();```<br>``````<br>```App({```<br>```    $$sdk,```<br>```    //...```<br>```    onLaunch() {```<br>```        // ...```<br>```        //Assuming that the set value is zhangsan, this value in real scenarios is generally obtained from the service interface of the business```<br>```        $$sdk.config({```<br>```            user_unique_id: 'zhangsan'```<br>```        });```<br>```    }```<br>```});```<br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">You can view the storage value of "_<em>tea_cache_tokens</em> ${app_id}" in the Storage panel under the Debugger in the Developer Tools, and you can see the value set to user_unique_id.</div><br> |<video src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/0a49ef27c6654be2a6fca5a692c226c3~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" controls></video><br> |



* Involving the core API: You can set the user's business identity ID through the config method \- user_unique_id, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder before setting it up (see details [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers)), and see more config interface introduction and parameter description [config](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#7fccc7c0).

* More scene practice references:

   * [user login settings](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice#e7ec629e)

<span id="d99c56a0"></span>
### Set up a reporting domain name

If your current environment is a SaaS\-cloud native environment or a private environment, you need to set the data reporting domain name of the corresponding environment, that is, set the channel_domain at initialization. If the settings are incorrect, the data will not be able to be queried and analyzed normally.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|```TypeScript```<br>```import $$sdk from '@datarangers/sdk-mp';```<br>``````<br>```$$sdk.init({```<br>```    //Please change to your own app_id```<br>```    app_id: 0,```<br>```    Assuming a cloud-native environment```<br>```    channel_domain: 'https://gator.uba.ap-southeast-1.bytepluses.com',```<br>```    log: true,```<br>```    auto_report: true,```<br>```});```<br>```$$sdk.send();```<br>``````<br>```App({```<br>```    $$sdk,```<br>```    //...```<br>```    onLaunch() {```<br>```        // ...```<br>```        //Assuming that the set value is zhangsan, this value in the real scenario is generally obtained from the service interface of the business```<br>```        $$sdk.config({```<br>```            user_unique_id: 'zhangsan'```<br>```        });```<br>```    }```<br>```});```<br> |<video src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/716d94be05f841e1a063b90f4ef0c3f1~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" controls></video><br> |



* Operation points: Before setting up a data reporting domain name, you need to clarify the environment and region you are using, and set the reporting domain name according to the actual situation. To confirm the type of environment you are currently using see: [SaaS Cloud-Native & Privatized Environments](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/SaaS_Cloud-Native_Privatized_Environments); see addresses for different environments [Step 3: Obtain the reporting address and configure the Mini Program whitelist](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration#f22345a9).

* Involving the core API: In the init interface, you can:

   * Only SaaS\-cloud native and privatized environments need to be set.

   * If you also open the A/B experiment scenario, you also need to configure the offload address (ab_channel_domain field) of the A/B experiment in the init interface according to the environment you use and the region you are located in.

      See more about the init interface and parameter descriptions [init](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#b83be19a).

## Step3: initialization result verification

<span id="6abd36ec"></span>
### Mini Program power builder

When initializing the SDK, you can enable `log: true`, which will print some running status information of the SDK on the console. Can be used to verify whether the initialization was successful


1. In the Console panel of the Mini Program power builder, filter by entering the `emit`keyword in the filter box. If there is a log of `emit $ready`, it means that the SDK initialization is successful.

   <div style="text-align: center">
   <img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/f869155cd2d749cea7535846a940b67e~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="946px" />   </div>
   

2. In the Network panel, you can see the event report request for the SDK, indicating that the SDK initialization was successful. At the same time, observe that the Request Payload of the request is normal, and the Response Body `message: "success"`indicates that the event was reported successfully.

   <div style="text-align: center">
   <img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/849031cd66c94a30842f83f87ea82c30~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="995px" />   </div>
   

   <div style="text-align: center">
   <img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/84fec94982c7402da8b172256f85e2ba~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="993px" />   </div>
   

3. In addition, in the Storage panel, you can see the token stored by the SDK, the key is called `__tea_cache_tokens_ ${app_id}`.

   <div style="text-align: center">
   <img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/57820fb8ea6f42b282b3d01314aeae41~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="1000px" />   </div>
   


<span id="a93e8abf"></span>
### Using DataFinder DevTools

`DevTools`is a component that assists developers or testers in the Debug environment to verify in\-app event tracking and troubleshoot SDK access issues. For detailed access documentation, please refer to: [Mini Program event tracking power builder ](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/76880/1033616).

<span id="7f7ebe90"></span>
## More scenarios in practice

<span id="a91178ad"></span>
### Capture and report custom user attributes

If you need to collect and report custom user attribute data, you need to open the corresponding parameter: `enable_profile: true`in the init interface when the SDK is initialized, and then call the user attribute module API to set it, see for details [User Attributes Module and API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#9b071c87).

<span id="f24b301b"></span>
### Capture and report element exposure events

If you want to capture the exposure time data of the element, you need to open the exposure capture ( `enable_exposure`) in the init interface when the SDK is initialized, and use the `exposure_config`method to set the specific parameters of the exposure capture. Please see for details [Element Exposure Module and API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#6590c90e).

<span id="f60167e1"></span>
### Setup Request Encryption

Currently supports the use of state secret encryption request, see details [Security compliance related](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice#69ad68e1).

<span id="dd144cba"></span>
### More scenarios in practice

See more scenario practice [Mini Program SDK Integration Scenario Practice](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice).

<span id="46f2518e"></span>
# Event tracking data validation

After completing the initialization verification, you can perform the test operation on the Mini Program side to trigger some events to be collected and reported. After the test event is reported, within about 15 minutes, you can view the specific user behavior flow data on the `user scrutiny`page in the `growth analysis platform`, that is, you can see the test event and event attribute data, which is used to verify whether the event tracking data can be collected and reported normally.


* The user behavior stream data displayed in the user scrutiny page usually has a fixed format, mainly including `user`, `header`, `events`three parts, which respectively display the user attribute data collected and reported, public event attribute, event and event attribute data. The reported data contains preset and custom data that are opened for collection.

* If the corresponding event can be seen in the user's investigation, it indicates that the event was successfully reported. By observing the properties of the event, it can be confirmed whether the corresponding attribute was also successfully reported.

* If the data is not found in the user scrutiny normally, you can check it:

   * Whether the data format of the reported data meets the requirements: [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

   * Check that the AppID in the integration code is correct [Import and initialize](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration#eaa78476).

   * For SaaS\-cloud native and privatized environments, check whether the reported domain name in the integration code is configured correctly: [Set up a reporting domain name](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration#d99c56a0).

      <div style="text-align: center">
      <img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/6c7a985fb3804a218b26ec91171cf2b2~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="2460px" />      </div>
      


<span id="5a102c32"></span>
# Mini Program SDK API List

DataFinder provides you with a wealth of API interfaces. In addition to the core interfaces and typical scenarios described in the above general process, you can also understand the main API interfaces supported by the current Mini Program and their functions. According to business needs, you can flexibly call the corresponding interface to complete the business tracking event.


|classification |API List |API Description |
|---|---|---|
|core API |[init](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#b83be19a) |API for initializing configuration of SDK instances. |
||[send](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#43b682a2) |After the init initialization call, the send method needs to be called before the SDK starts reporting events. No events are reported until the send method is called. |
||[config](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#7fccc7c0) |Call config to make some settings for the event, such as setting public properties, setting user_unique_id, etc. It can be called multiple times, and subsequent settings will override the same previous settings. |
||[event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#68e73ad4) |Use the event method to report custom events. |
|non\-core API |[setUserUniqueID](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#43c874f6) |Set user_unique_id, which can be called multiple times, and later settings will overwrite the same settings as before.<br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Using the setUserUniqueID interface to set user_unique_id the same as using the config interface to set user_unique_id effect. In fact, the setUserUniqueID interface is also a config method called internally. Providing a separate setUserUniqueID can satisfy some scenarios where the client side directly calls the API to set user_unique_id.</div><br> |
||[setHeaderInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#a608d39d) |Set the event public property, which can be called multiple times, and subsequent settings will override the same previous settings.<br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Using the setHeaderInfo interface to set public properties is the same as using the config interface to set public properties. In fact, the setHeaderInfo interface is also a config method called internally. Providing a separate setHeaderInfo can satisfy some scenarios where the client side directly calls the API to set public properties.</div><br> |
||[removeHeaderInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#73b75e64) |Removes event public properties. |
||[disableSDK](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#a9dfd686) |Pause SDK reporting events. After calling this method, the SDK will be suspended and no events will be reported in the future. |
||[enableSDK](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#42d29839) |Cancel the suspension of SDK reporting, usually after calling the disableSDK and planning to cancel the suspension, that is, restart the SDK reporting, and the reporting event will be resumed later. |
|Module API |[AB test Modules and APIs](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#e15ecfb8) |This module provides AB test capabilities and provides a range of methods: `getVar`, `getAllVars`, `getAbSdkVersion`, `setExternalAbVersion`. |
||[User Attributes Module and API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#9b071c87) |This module provides the ability to set user properties and provides a series of methods: `profileSet`, `profileSetOnce`, `profileUnset`, `profileIncrement`, `profileAppend`. |
||[Element Exposure Module and API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_API_Description#6590c90e) |This module provides the ability to set exposure capture, supports setting whether to turn on exposure capture ( `enable_exposure`), and provides `exposure_config`methods for setting specific parameter configuration items for exposure capture. |

# Related operations

<span id="e5b10dbf"></span>
## Console cloud control configuration

SaaS cloud native version or privatization V4.4.0 or above, DataFinder supports SDK settings through server level distribution, including reporting timing, full event tracking switch, etc. Please refer to the detailed introduction document: [Project Management - SDK Settings](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Project_Management_-_SDK_Settings). The following is the initialization configuration of the Mini Program SDK during initialization, and you can also adjust the configuration later in the DataFinder console.
